body: Leveraging their inherent sparse event-driven computation, spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a promising path toward energy-efficient large language models (LLMs). Time-to-first-spike (TTFS) coding generates at most one spike per neuron within a time window, yielding extremely low firing rates. However, conventional TTFS SNNs are restricted to specific structures, making it challenging to encode certain blocks in LLM -- such as layer normalization and matrix multiplication --using TTFS. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a reference-based strategy specifically to encode the four core LLM components: embedding layers, layer normalization, attention-related operations and dropout. We construct a fully TTFS-based SNN architecture and train it end-to-end. Experiments on modern LLMs like BERT and GPT-2 demonstrate that our approach achieves performance comparable to ANN counterparts on natural language understanding and common-sense reasoning, while a clear gap remains on language modeling perplexity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to scale a spiking LLM to 1.5 billion parameters using TTFS coding. We also report an estimate of spike-related energy; this is a spike-count proxy under an established cost model rather than a measurement on neuromorphic hardware.
summaryZh: 为了探索大语言模型的节能计算路径，本文研究了基于脉冲神经网络（SNNs）的大模型。通过采用首次发放时间（TTFS）编码策略，并在嵌入层、层归一化、注意力和丢弃层四大核心组件上应用参考基础策略，成功将脉冲大语言模型扩展至15亿参数规模。在自然语言理解和常识推理任务上，该方法实现了与人工神经网络相当的性能。

glossary.explanationZh: 脉冲神经网络，一种模仿生物神经元脉冲发放、具备高能效特性的神经网络
首次发放时间编码，通过限制每个神经元在时间窗口内最多发射一个脉冲实现极低发放率
层归一化技术，用于稳定深度神经网络的训练过程
困惑度，衡量语言模型预测文本能力的经典统计指标
